extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers of analytic geometry / conic sections (advanced undergraduate/graduate level)
extracted.subtask_description: Derive and apply algebraic properties of polar reciprocals of conic sections (and related constructions): general formulae, special cases (circle, parabola, hyperbola), loci of poles, tangent construction, and related integral/constructive results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity implies polar-reciprocal intersection lines and harmonic pencil
rubrics_metrics.description: When two conic sections are similar, their polar reciprocals intersect on two straight lines which pass through the pole of the straight line joining the centres of the two given curves; and those conjugate common secants together with the polars of these centres form a harmonic pencil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to any pair of similar conics; identifies the geometric locus (two straight lines) of intersection of their reciprocals and the harmonic relation among the common secants and polars of the centres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common pole for system of similar conics with collinear centres
rubrics_metrics.description: If a system of similar conic sections have their centres in the same straight line, the pole of that line is a point of intersection of conjugate common secants for any two of their reciprocal curves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If many similar conics share a common centre-line, that line's pole is a universal intersection point of conjugate common secants of any two reciprocals from the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentric conics: centre of director as intersection point of conjugate common secants
rubrics_metrics.description: The polar reciprocals of any two concentric conic sections have the centre of the director for a point of intersection of conjugate common secants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the two original conics are concentric, their reciprocals intersect in lines through the director's centre; lines may be real or imaginary depending on coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: General method for finding polar reciprocal of a conic (director is a conic)
rubrics_metrics.description: To find the polar reciprocal of any curve of the second degree with respect to any other curve of the second degree taken as director: write director (eq. 8) and given curve (eq. 9); let (x',y') be a point on the given curve and (x,y) the corresponding point on the reciprocal; equate the tangent at (x',y') to the polar at (x,y), form the resulting linear relations and eliminate x',y' (using the given curve) to obtain the equation of the reciprocal (e.g., general form (10)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithmic recipe: (1) write tangent to given curve at (x',y'); (2) write polar of (x,y) wrt director; (3) set lines identical → obtain linear equations; (4) denote second members as −X,−Y and follow elimination to yield the reciprocal's equation. Final resulting equation is typically quartic in coefficients but reduces in special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director circle/equilateral hyperbola centre at focus gives reciprocal circle
rubrics_metrics.description: When the director is either a circle or an equilateral hypertola, if its centre be at a focus of the given curve the reciprocal curve is a circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebraic conditions: FB − DE = 0 and D² − AF = E² − CF (plus C' = +A' for the reciprocal to be a circle in the derived formulae). Use when director is circle or equilateral hyperbola and its centre coincides with a focus of the given conic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugate-diameter/asymptote parallelism condition
rubrics_metrics.description: If D' − AF = 0 then the given curve touches the axis of x, and the reciprocal is a hyperbola having an asymptote parallel to the axis of y; hence if a diameter of the director be drawn touching one of the curves, its conjugate diameter will be parallel to an asymptote of the other curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates contact of a curve with a director's axis to asymptotic directions of its reciprocal; used when reciprocal curves are referred to conjugate diameters of the director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic director: reciprocal equation (parabola case)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the director is a parabola (assume A'=0, B'=0, C'=1, D'=1, E'=0, F'=0), the reciprocal curve's equation reduces to (12): (B' − AC) x'² + 2(BD − AE) x' y' + (D' − AF) y'² + 2(CD − BE) x' + 2(DE − FB) y' + E' − FC = 0 (specialized form given in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this simplified form to derive many parabolic reciprocal properties; subsequent numbered properties (1st–8th) follow from special vanishing conditions of coefficient combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic reciprocal property 1: asymptote parallel to director axis
rubrics_metrics.description: When B'² − AC = 0 the reciprocal curve has an asymptote parallel to the axis of x; hence when one of the curves is a parabola, the other has an asymptote parallel to the axis of the director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition B'² − AC = 0 detects asymptotic parallelism between reciprocal curves and director axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic reciprocal property 2: centre alignment and conjugate diameters
rubrics_metrics.description: When BD − AE = 0 the centre of the given curve is on the axis of x, and the reciprocal curve has a system of conjugate diameters parallel to the axes of x and y; thus if a diameter of the director be drawn through the centre of one reciprocal curve, the other curve has conjugate diameters respectively parallel to that diameter and to the tangent at the vertex of the director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interprets BD−AE=0 as the centre of one curve lying on the director's axis, producing axis-parallel systems of conjugate diameters in the reciprocal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic reciprocal property 3: touch/asymptote correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: When D² − AF = 0 the given curve touches the axis of x, and the reciprocal curve has an asymptote parallel to the axis of y; hence if a diameter of the director be drawn touching one of the curves, the tangent applied to the director at the vertex of that diameter is parallel to an asymptote of the other curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use D² − AF = 0 to deduce tangency/asymptote parallel relations between reciprocal curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic reciprocal property 4: contact and passant through origin
rubrics_metrics.description: When E² − FC = 0 the given curve touches the axis of y, and the reciprocal passes through the origin; consequently if a common tangent is applied to the given curve and the director, the reciprocal curve passes through the point in which it touches the director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detects conditions under which a common tangent yields a point of passage of the reciprocal through the origin (relative to coordinates chosen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic reciprocal property 5: centre on director gives diameter relation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the centre of the given curve is at the origin (D = 0, E = 0), the reciprocal is a conic with a specified axis; hence when the centre of the given curve is on the director, the tangent to the director at that point is a diameter of the reciprocal curve, and the diameter of the director which passes through the point of contact is parallel to its conjugate diameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vanishing of D and E to detect the centre-on-director situation and associated diameter/polar correspondences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic reciprocal property 6: common contact points
rubrics_metrics.description: When the given curve passes through the origin and touches the axis of y (E = 0, F = 0) then the reciprocal is a conic touching the axis of y at the origin; hence when one of the reciprocal curves touches the director at any point, the other touches it at the same point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows reciprocity of contact points with the director under these coefficient vanishing conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic reciprocal property 7: parallel axes produce parabolic reciprocal
rubrics_metrics.description: When A = 0 and B = 0 (given curve is a parabola with axis parallel to the director) the reciprocal curve is also a parabola whose axis is parallel to the axis of the director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives condition for parabolic-to-parabolic reciprocity preserving axis directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabolic reciprocal property 8: polar-of-centre equals diameter bisecting chords
rubrics_metrics.description: The equation of the diameter of (12) which bisects chords parallel to the axis of x is (B' − AC) x' − (BD − AE) y' + CD − BE = 0; the polar of the centre of one curve with respect to the director coincides with the diameter of the other which bisects chords parallel to the axis of the director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies explicit diameter equation and asserts coincidence with the polar of the centre—useful for constructing reciprocal diameters and centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentric conics wrt parabola: reciprocals intersect on two lines parallel to parabola axis
rubrics_metrics.description: If two conic sections are concentric, their polar reciprocals with respect to any parabola intersect each other on two straight lines parallel to the axis of the parabola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from comparing equations (12') and (14) when A,A' and B,B' correspond to concentric configuration; useful for symmetry arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common focus at parabola vertex implies common secant touching parabola
rubrics_metrics.description: If any system of conic sections have the principal vertex of a parabola for a common focus, the polar reciprocals of any two of them, taken with respect to the parabola, have a common secant which touches the parabola at that vertex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for a point being a common focus translate into the reciprocals sharing a secant tangent to the director parabola at its vertex; verification via algebraic elimination of variables as shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locus of pole of chord subtending fixed angle: general quartic and special conic cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two radii vectors from a fixed point making a given angle, the locus of the pole of the chord connecting their extremities is in general a curve of the fourth degree (quartic); in special cases it reduces to a conic or line (e.g., right angle → conic; point on curve → conic; vertex at focus → conic; right angle + point on curve sometimes → straight line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General derivation proceeds by eliminating parameters from chord equations and tangent/pole relations; see equation (16) and subsequent specializations (18) etc. Interpret special algebraic vanishing conditions (e.g., F = 0, φ = 0) to detect reductions in degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectangular radii (right angle) case: locus and envelope are conics
rubrics_metrics.description: If two rectangular radii vectors be drawn from a fixed point in the plane of a conic section, the locus of the pole of the chord connecting their extremities is a conic section, and the envelope of the chord is also a conic section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use substitution φ = 0 (right angle) in general locus equation to obtain (18); both locus and envelope are conics and can be written explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-on-curve case: locus is a conic with double contact and conic envelope
rubrics_metrics.description: If the given point (vertex of the angle) lies on the conic (F = 0), then the locus of the pole of the chord subtending the fixed angle is a second-degree curve (conic) which has a double contact with the given conic, and its envelope is also a conic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute F = 0 into (16) to obtain second-degree equation in parameters; when angle is right the locus may degenerate to the chord-of-contact line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus-vertex case: fixed-angle vertex at a focus gives conic locus
rubrics_metrics.description: If the vertex of the variable angle coincides with a focus of the given curve (satisfying E' − CF = D' − AF and DE − BF = 0), the locus of the pole is a conic section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the focus conditions the quartic reduces algebraically to a conic by solving for auxiliary quantities (G constant in derivation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Method XIV: general polar reciprocal of arbitrary given curve wrt conic director
rubrics_metrics.description: To find the polar reciprocal of a given curve w = 0 with respect to any curve of the second degree taken as director: let (x',y') be a point on w = 0 and (x,y) the corresponding point of the reciprocal; write the polar of (x,y) wrt director and the tangent to w at (x',y'), set them identical to obtain linear relations, and eliminate x',y' using w' = 0 to obtain the equation of the reciprocal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit equations (19),(20) in the text show how to equate coefficients and eliminate; this is the canonical procedure applicable to arbitrary given w and conic director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example theorem for parabola director: contact and diameter correspondences
rubrics_metrics.description: If any tangent be applied to the given parabola, the reciprocal curve (wrt a parabola director) touches the polar of the point of contact and the diameter of the director which bisects chords parallel to the axis of the parabola; and the straight line joining the points of contact is the diameter of the director which bisects chords parallel to the tangent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Example 1 derivation where reciprocal curve equation reduces and yields tangency points: specifically, the reciprocal touches the polar of contact point and the appropriate diameter of the director.

rubrics_metrics.name: New method for equation of tangent to conic sections (Maclaurin elimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place origin at vertex A and represent conic in form (1 − e²) x² − 2(1+e) m x + k y² = 0 (or equivalent); take point (h,k) on curve, form linear combination (2) and eliminate x between (1) and (3) to obtain equation (4), which is tangential to curve. Specializations give explicit tangent forms for parabola, ellipse, hyperbola (equations (5),(6),(7) and centered forms (6'),(7')).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a uniform algebraic procedure to obtain tangent equation at a given point without indeterminate expressions; plug in eccentricity e and focal distance m to compute concrete tangent formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of ± in perpendicular distance formula
rubrics_metrics.description: In the perpendicular distance formula from a point to a line, the double sign should be chosen according as the point lies above or below the line: use the upper sign when the point is above the line (ordinate larger than intersection ordinate), and the lower sign when below, so that the distance p is positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained by comparing ordinates: if k − a h − b is positive (point above line AB) take + sign; if negative take − sign. This removes ambiguity in the algebraic expression for perpendicular distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maclaurin-series by successive differentiation for circular functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop circular functions (e.g., tan x, sec x) by pure successive differentiation (no binomial/indeterminate coefficient methods), derive recurrence relations for higher derivatives (expressions for the n-th derivative in terms of lower ones), and compute Maclaurin coefficients U_n for series expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives explicit recurrences, example first coefficients and shows algorithmic differentiation and rearrangement to get general coefficient formulas; practical for computing series to any order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction: place conic with given centre and major axis tangent to two lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an angle and a point within it and the major axis magnitude, to place a conic so its centre is the given point and the two lines are tangents: draw circle centered at given point with radius equal to semi-major axis, intersections with tangents are feet of perpendiculars from foci; draw perpendiculars at these points to find foci intersections; then curve determined by foci and major axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction yields up to two solutions (ellipse/hyperbola combinations) depending on relative positions of foci and circle; degenerate cases considered when foci separation equals major axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume and centroid of conical sector over surface z=f(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed curve director on surface z = f(x,y) and a conical sector with apex at origin, the volume and coordinates of centre of gravity are V = (1/3) ∫ (z − p x − q y) dA, V x_bar = (1/4) ∫ x (z − p x − q y) dA etc., where p = ∂z/∂x, q = ∂z/∂y evaluated at the surface point; integration over the projection of the curve. The integrand (z − p x − q y) must not change sign over the domain (else subdivide).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivation uses elemental cones of height proportional to distance from origin to tangent plane; sign convention ensures positive perpendicular P; if tangent planes meet z-axis on both sides of origin, subdivide region so integrand sign is constant before integrating.
